processes.process: Manual stripping of cork-oak bark with a single hand axe (machado): a vertical incision in the deepest fissure, axe edge twisted between layers to pry the cork off, a horizontal cut sizing the sheet, peeled carefully to avoid splitting.
processes.inefficiency: Stripping is undertaken by specialised professionals with absolute precision; success depends entirely on the harvester's skill, and cutting too deep damages the cambium (harming the tree); the larger the intact sheet, the higher its commercial value.
processes.inefficiency_quote: Success depends entirely on the harvester's skill.
processes.ai_amenable_note: depth-of-cut guidance / cork-cambium boundary sensing / bark-readiness + sheet-size optimization via CV or robotics

processes.process: Each Crocus sativus flower yields only three crimson stigmas; the stigmas must be individually plucked by hand before/just after sunrise, then dried.
processes.inefficiency: One of the most labor-intensive agricultural processes in the world; mechanical harvesting is not an option because machines easily crush or contaminate the threads; ~440,000 hand-picked stigmas per kilogram; growers may work 19-hour days.
processes.inefficiency_quote: mechanical harvesting is not an option-machines can easily crush or contaminate the precious threads
processes.ai_amenable_note: CV stigma detection + delicate (soft) robotic micro-manipulation -- precisely where CRUDE mechanization failed

processes.process: Traditional earth-mound (earth kiln) pyrolysis: logs stacked in a conical mound covered with earth, with base air vents and a central chimney; carbonization regulated and monitored by smoke-color changes from white to blue/clear.
processes.inefficiency: Workers maintain 24/7 observation tracking smoke-color changes as the key indicator of pyrolysis stage; traditional earth-mound kilns achieve only ~15-25% yield (70-80% of the wood's energy lost as smoke/gas/heat).
processes.inefficiency_quote: workers maintain constant vigilance through 24/7 observation to monitor the carbonization process
processes.ai_amenable_note: CV smoke-color/plume classification + low-cost gas/temperature sensors + ML to detect pyrolysis stage and control vents -> raise yield, cut emissions, end 24/7 manual watching

processes.process: Separating bast fibre from non-fibrous plant material by microbial or chemical degradation of the cementing compounds (pectin) that bind the fibres, followed by mechanical breaking and scutching.
processes.inefficiency: Retting endpoint is judged by feel/experience; under-retting leaves fibres bound, over-retting weakens/dirties them; quality and timing vary widely with method (pond/stream/field) and conditions.
processes.inefficiency_quote: The separation is primarily achieved through either a microbial or chemical action degradating the cementing compounds that bind the bast fibres
processes.ai_amenable_note: CV/hyperspectral or microbial-sensor ML to detect the optimal retting endpoint (avoid over/under-retting)

processes.process: Cooking and steeping maize in an alkaline lime solution (pH > 11) to dissolve hemicellulose, loosen hulls, partially solubilize proteins/cell walls and facilitate starch swelling; then washed and hulled.
processes.inefficiency: Cooking time and steeping (minutes to ~a day) and alkalinity are set empirically; over/under-cooking changes texture, nutrition (niacin release), and downstream dough quality; control is largely manual/experiential.
processes.inefficiency_quote: cooking times ranging from a few minutes to an hour, and soaking times from a few minutes to about a day
processes.ai_amenable_note: process-control ML (online pH/turbidity/texture sensing) or CV doneness estimation to standardize the endpoint

processes.process: Cocoon sorting before industrial reeling: grading cocoons (ISC A-E by filament length/reelability) and separating defects (stained, double, malformed, Uzi-fly-pierced) plus silkworm disease detection.
processes.inefficiency: Cocoon sorting is one of the most labor-demanding steps and 'automatization is mandatory to reduce silk costs'; Uzi-fly infestation can reach 80% of silkworms in affected regions.
processes.inefficiency_quote: automatization of this production step is mandatory to reduce silk costs and standardize fiber quality
processes.ai_amenable_note: CV cocoon grading + CNN silkworm disease detection -- INCLUDED DELIBERATELY AS THE ALREADY-AI'D CONTRAST (PHASE 2 should show HIGH penetration)
